Q: How to solve the final test case of HackerRank's Gemstone problem A:

The final test case usually fails because the solution checks character frequency instead of character presence.
A gemstone is defined as a character that appears at least once in every string, not multiple times in one string.

Correct approach

  1. Convert each string into a set to remove duplicate characters

  2. Find the intersection of all sets

  3. Count the remaining common characters

Python solution

def gemstones(arr):
    common = set(arr[0])

    for rock in arr[1:]:
        common &= set(rock)

    return len(common)

Why this passes the final test case

  • set() removes duplicates automatically

  • Set intersection ensures the character exists in all strings

  • Time complexity is efficient: O(n × m)
    where n is the number of strings and m is the maximum string length

Common mistakes that cause failure

  • Counting characters instead of checking presence

  • Not removing duplicates within a string

  • Using nested loops that lead to time-limit issues

Note

For problems that require finding common elements across multiple inputs, using set intersection is the most reliable and optimized approach.

Q: How do I get actual jar file and translator for J2ObjC? A:

This page has instructions for building j2objc from source code (on MacOS):

  • https://developers.google.com/j2objc/guides/building-j2objc

j2objc is only supported on iOS/macOS, so you won't find a BAT file for it. But the Github site includes instructions on running the tool on Linux.

(Apparently some of the build artifacts are published on Maven Central with groupId of com.google.j2objc, but AFAIK this doesn't include the JARs for the tool itself.)

Q: How to display two(current and max) values in Grafana A:

I might be misunderstanding the question, but from what I read, you want 2 results shown up against each other.

Why not just create a dashboard with 2 singlestats, each representing a query. A graph is easily also an option if you want both queries displayed and visualized on the same display (just create a query A and query B).

For inspiration check out the official demo-site for prometheus on Grafana: https://play.grafana.org/d/000000029/prometheus-demo-dashboard?orgId=1&refresh=5m

If that's not what you are looking for, then please specify, and I will gladly help.

Update in response to comment

Alright, if you want to perform arithmetic operations then the MetaQueries plugin is definitely an option. Check out the documentation: https://grafana.com/grafana/plugins/goshposh-metaqueries-datasource

Also you can check out the documentation in regards to arithmetic operations using prometheus: https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/operators/

TL;DR you've stated that you have the queries ready - have you tried using the '/' (division) operator?
